findings.title: Raw SQL Syntax Error Leakage on /api/vulnerable/users
findings.evidence:
Database error signature matched: /you have an error in your sql syntax/i
Response snippet: {"error":"Internal Database Error","sql_message":"You have an error in your SQL syntax; check the manual that corresponds to your MySQL server version for the right syntax to use near ''' at line 1","query":"SELECT id, username, email FROM users WHER
reproduction_steps: Observe HTTP 500 with unhandled SQL error syntax disclosure
findings.impact: Critical. Attackers can extract complete database contents, bypass access controls, or tamper with business data.
findings.remediation: Replace string concatenation with parameterized prepared statements (e.g. db.query(sql, [param])).
findings.cwe_ref: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command

findings.title: Boolean Query Response Disparity on /api/vulnerable/users
findings.evidence: True payload returned 95 bytes; False payload returned 95 bytes.
reproduction_steps: Submit 1' AND '1'='2 -> returns empty set or error
findings.impact: Enables blind SQL inference of database records character-by-character.
findings.remediation: Use strict type casting and prepared statements.

findings.title: Query Parameters Safely Bound on /api/secure/users
findings.evidence: Status: 200. No SQL parse signatures encountered.
findings.impact: Parameters properly bounded.
findings.remediation: Maintain parameterized query practices.

findings.title: Authentication Bypass via SQL Injection on /api/vulnerable/login
findings.evidence: Bypass payload granted authenticated session without valid password: {"success":true,"message":"Authentication successful","user":{"id":1,"username":"alice","role":"user"}}
reproduction_steps: Submit POST to /api/vulnerable/login with username: "admin' OR '1'='1' -- "
findings.impact: Critical. Attackers can log in as administrator or arbitrary users without knowing their password.
findings.remediation: Validate credentials using parameterized SELECT WHERE username = ? and compare hashed password via bcrypt.

findings.title: Authentication Input Properly Handled on /api/secure/login
findings.evidence: Rejected with status 401: {"success":false,"message":"Invalid username or password"}
reproduction_steps: Submitted SQL injection payload to login endpoint
findings.impact: Protected against SQL authentication bypass.
findings.remediation: Maintain secure parameterization and password hashing.

findings.title: State-Changing Operation Executable via HTTP GET on /api/vulnerable/transfer
findings.evidence: HTTP GET triggered state mutation: {"success":true,"message":"Transferred $1 to audit_test (VULNERABLE: No CSRF token or origin check)","recipient":"audit_test","amount":1}
reproduction_steps: Notice endpoint executes transaction without requiring POST or CSRF validation
findings.impact: High. An attacker can execute arbitrary state changes by embedding the URL in a simple on a third-party webpage.
findings.remediation: Disallow GET on state-changing endpoints. Enforce POST/PUT with CSRF tokens.

findings.title: State-Changing POST Accepted Without CSRF Token on /api/vulnerable/transfer
findings.evidence: POST succeeded without X-CSRF-Token or CSRF form parameter: HTTP 200 OK
reproduction_steps: Send POST to http://localhost:3000/api/vulnerable/transfer with session cookie but omit CSRF token
findings.impact: Enables cross-origin sites to forge actions on behalf of authenticated users.
findings.remediation: Implement anti-CSRF token middleware (e.g., csrf-csrf or csurf) and require custom headers for API calls.

findings.title: Session Cookie Lacks SameSite Restriction on /api/vulnerable/transfer
findings.evidence: Set-Cookie: session_id=vulnerable-session-token-12345; Path=/; HttpOnly
reproduction_steps: Verify absence of SameSite=Lax or SameSite=Strict
findings.impact: Cookies are attached to cross-site requests, increasing vulnerability to CSRF.
findings.remediation: Configure SameSite=Lax or SameSite=Strict in cookie options: res.cookie(name, val, { sameSite: "lax", httpOnly: true, secure: true }).

findings.title: Anti-CSRF Token Enforced on /api/secure/transfer
findings.evidence: Request without token rejected with HTTP 403: {"error":"Forbidden: Missing or invalid CSRF token"}
findings.impact: Cross-site forgery prevented by anti-CSRF validation.
findings.remediation: Keep CSRF tokens required on all non-safe HTTP methods.

findings.title: Arbitrary Origin Reflected with Credentials Allowed on /api/vulnerable/profile
findings.evidence: Origin: https://unauthorized-attacker.test reflected in Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://unauthorized-attacker.test with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true
reproduction_steps: Send GET to http://localhost:3000/api/vulnerable/profile with header 'Origin: https://unauthorized-attacker.test'
Verify response contains 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://unauthorized-attacker.test' and 'Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true'
findings.impact: High. Untrusted external web origins can read sensitive user data and bypass browser SOP.
findings.remediation: Replace dynamic origin reflection with a static allowlist of trusted origins.

findings.title: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) on User Profile API
findings.evidence: Record retrieved without session ownership check: {"id":99,"username":"admin","email":"admin.demo@example.test","role":"admin","balance":10000,"password_hash":"$2b$10$EixZaYVK1fsbw1ZfbX3OXePaWxn96p36WQoeG6Lruj3vjPGga31lW"}
reproduction_steps: Observe full user object returned despite lack of administrator privileges
findings.impact: High. Allows any caller to enumerate and read sensitive profile records belonging to other users.
findings.remediation: Verify that req.session.userId === requestedUserId or check ownership in the database query.
findings.cwe_ref: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key
